blocking.issue: This is a new regression in text added by this revision. The gRPC proxying design registers one generic connect bidirectional-stream handler per procedure and says no descriptor is needed. connect-go chooses which content types a handler accepts from the handler's stream type. A handler built with NewBidiStreamHandler accepts only enveloped streaming content types (application/connect+proto, application/grpc, application/grpc-web). It rejects Connect-protocol unary requests (Content-Type application/proto, or HTTP GET), and those are the default calls that Connect clients make. So the design as written cannot serve one of the three protocols the foundation pack fixes for gRPC ingress ('gRPC, gRPC-Web, Connect on net/http'). There is a second gap. Turning Upstream grpc-status into 'client trailers' is right only for gRPC. For Connect unary and gRPC-Web, the handler must return a *connect.Error with the mapped code and details so that connect-go writes the protocol's own error encoding. Raw trailers written by a pass-through codec yield a successful response with a wrong or empty body.
blocking.evidence: gRPC proxying: "Each Route-derived procedure (`/pkg.Service/Method` or a service prefix) gets a generic connect bidirectional-stream handler whose codec passes message bytes through unparsed. gRPC, gRPC-Web and Connect with protobuf encoding carry identical bytes, so no descriptor is needed." and "Upstream `grpc-status`, `grpc-message` and trailing metadata become client trailers."
blocking.fix: For each Route-derived procedure, register two generic connect handlers, one unary (NewUnaryHandler with the pass-through codec) and one bidi. Put a small Ruralz http.Handler in front that sends application/proto, application/json and GET Connect requests to the unary handler, and every enveloped content type to the bidi handler. This keeps the design descriptor-free, because the Connect content type itself marks a unary call. Change 'so no descriptor is needed' to 'no message descriptor is needed; the stream type comes from the Content-Type'. State that a non-OK Upstream grpc-status is returned from the handler as *connect.Error (code, message, details from grpc-status-details-bin), and that trailing metadata on success goes to the response trailers. Add 'Connect unary and error mapping' to the scope of OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-21 so the spike covers it. Keep the addition short, because the body is already about 3,990 words against the 4,000-word maximum.

non_blocking.section: Go toolchain, static builds and FIPS
non_blocking.suggestion: Version floor: 'plain `go build` and `go install` need no flags' holds inside the module. It does not hold for `go install github.com/ravindu-rev/ruralz/cmd/ruralzd@vX` on Go 1.26, where the toolchain directive of a non-main module does not trigger a switch, so the guard file fails the build. Say that the `@version` form needs Go 1.27 or GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2.

non_blocking.suggestion: FIPS build, JOSE row: neither GOFIPS140=v1.0.0 (frozen from Go 1.24) nor v1.26.0 contains ML-DSA, so in a FIPS build crypto/mldsa is outside the selected validated module even on Go 1.27. State that ML-DSA JWA algorithms are not registered in FIPS builds until a validated module version includes ML-DSA.

non_blocking.section: Go toolchain, static builds and FIPS
non_blocking.suggestion: G3 check: a denylist keyed on 'crypto' in the import path will not see primitives or constructions in packages named otherwise, for example go-jose/v4's `cipher` package (AES key wrap, concat KDF, ECDH-ES). 'The G3 check decides' for go-jose/v4, OPA and sigstore-go therefore needs an explicit per-module allowlist review, not the path heuristic alone. Say so in the G3 exception table or in OQ-9.

The claim that Ruralz Control and the CLI surface GraphQL errors in `ruralz bundle validate` rests on importing only `ast` and `astvalidation`. Research lists no federation composition component in graphql-go-tools v2, so supergraph composition errors may still surface only in Node-side planning. Limit the claim to schema and operation validation, or add composition to OQ-22.
